title: AI-enhanced seismic catalog exposes a ring-fault system at Campi Flegrei
summary: A retrained machine-learning workflow applied to continuous seismic records from 2022–2025 expanded the Campi Flegrei earthquake catalog from about 12,000 to more than 54,000 events. The more complete locations delineated a sharply defined, shallow caldera ring-fault system, illuminated previously unclear northern faults, and identified very shallow hybrid events likely associated with the hydrothermal system. The authors report no direct signature of upward magma migration in the analyzed data.
ai_technology: Retrained machine-learning seismic detection and phase-picking workflow developed at Stanford
organization: Stanford University; Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia – Osservatorio Vesuviano; University of Naples Federico II

evidence.tested: A retrained machine-learning workflow applied to continuous seismic records from 2022–2025 expanded the Campi Flegrei earthquake catalog from about 12,000 to more than 54,000 events.
evidence.unknown: The observations cover 21 January 2022–20 March 2025. The inferred hydrothermal source is described as likely, and the mapped faults do not establish imminent eruption or earthquake timing. Full Science article text was access-restricted in this review; the original abstract and reporting institution's article were read.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and located small earthquakes missed by the prior monitoring catalog, providing denser observations that made the ring-fault geometry and shallow seismic structures visible.
